tip: Bydd is the future of bod for 'he/she/it'. Add yn before the verb: Bydd y siop yn cau (the shop will close).
Byddwn ni = we will (future). Swap ni for i and Byddwn i means 'I would' (conditional). The pronoun sets the meaning.
Welsh says half past as hanner awr wedi tri, literally 'half an hour past three'. Here wedi means 'past'.
For writing or sending to a person, Welsh uses at, not i: llythyr at ei mam-gu (a letter to her grandmother).
The word yn (in) becomes ym before m: ym mis Medi (in September).
Pe bai means 'if... were', for unreal or hypothetical situations: Pe bai'r trên ar amser (if the train were on time).
byddwch chi = you will, for a group or a polite 'you': gobeithio byddwch chi'n mwynhau (hope you'll enjoy).
Pe gallwn i means 'if I could', the conditional of gallu (to be able): Pe gallwn i goginio (if I could cook).
The -wch ending makes a command plural or polite: Sefwch means 'stand' to a group or formally.
Welsh has no verb 'have'. Mae gen i means 'I have', literally 'there is with me': Mae gen i anifail anwes.
After the 'have' word ganddo, the owned thing soft-mutates: ci (dog) becomes gi in Mae ganddo fo gi du.
Reported 'that... not' uses na plus mutation: byddai turns into na fyddai (that she wouldn't) after Addawodd hi.
After â in a command, p becomes ph: poeni turns into Paid â phoeni (don't worry).
cymer is the informal singular command 'take', from cymryd: cymer dy amser (take your time).
cystal is the special 'as good as' form of da, used with â: cystal â'r llyfr (as good as the book).
'Near' pairs with at, not i: yn agos at y llyfrgell (near the library).
Welsh 'to rain' is bwrw glaw, literally 'to strike rain': Bydd hi'n bwrw glaw (it will rain).
mor (as/so) soft-mutates the next word: prydferth becomes brydferth in mor brydferth â llun (as beautiful as a painting).
Add -ach for 'more' and follow with na for 'than': yn flasusach na bwyd y caffi (tastier than the café food).
Peidiwch â is the plural or polite 'don't'; Paid â is for one person: Peidiwch â bwydo (don't feed).
